suggested_experiment_name: Inverse-Square-Law Tests (ISL) — Casimir Force, Torsion Balance, Lunar Laser Ranging
coupling_convention: α(λ), dimensionless Yukawa coupling strength (inverse-square-law violation parameter)
notes: This is a comprehensive review article (arXiv:hep-ph/0307284) on experimental tests of the gravitational inverse-square law by Adelberger, Heckel, and Nelson. It discusses theoretical motivations (extra dimensions, new bosons, cosmological constant) and summarizes existing experimental results from torsion oscillators, microcantilevers, Casimir-force experiments, and astronomical tests. The paper does NOT present new measured exclusion limits or sensitivity projections from a single experiment. Instead, it reviews and compiles results from multiple prior experiments (e.g., Eöt-Wash group, Colorado group, Stanford microcantilever, lunar laser ranging). The figures (4, 5, 9, 10) show compilations of constraints on Yukawa-type fifth-force parameters (α vs λ), but these are summaries of previously published work, not new data. The paper is theoretical/review in nature and does not introduce a new coupling type relevant to axion or dark photon searches. The excluded region (yellow) is ABOVE the boundary curves. The lower boundary of the exclusion region has been traced from left to right, sampling more densely at corners (e.g., around the Casimir force transition near 1 μm and the Lamoreaux/Stanford constraints). The coupling type is ScalarNucleon because the paper discusses Yukawa-type fifth forces and equivalence principle tests (ISL violations). The plot combines experimental constraints from Lamoreaux (torsion balance), Stanford (microcantilever), Moscow, Colorado, Irvine, and Eotvos-Wash experiments.
